reply_text:
*I would hold the merge.* Two rollout-safety issues in `e3396ff`:

1. *CRITICAL — Rules leak between flags* — `flags/registry.py:13–15`
   The mutable default `rules=[]` is shared by every two-argument `add_rule()` call. Creating an EU rule for `public-beta` also enables an earlier staff-only flag for free EU users. I reproduced both flags sharing the same rules object.
   *Recommended fix:* allocate a fresh list per call; copy supplied rules before appending to avoid mutating existing flags. Add an independence regression test—the current registry tests always supply explicit lists, masking the default-list bug.

2. *CRITICAL — Normalization changes targeting beyond the documented string/integer support* — `flags/match.py:2`
   Stringifying every value makes a missing field match the literal `"none"`: `matches({'region': 'none'}, {})` now returns `True`. It also breaks previously valid numeric equality: rule `{'tier': 1}` against context `{'tier': 1.0}` changes from `True` to `False`. Both reproduced against `main`.
   *Recommended fix:* distinguish absent fields and normalize only supported types, preserving existing equality where intended. Add missing-field, null/boolean, and numeric compatibility tests.

All five existing tests pass. Reviewed the full diff and all in-repo consumers; external consumers weren’t available in this checkout. *No code changed.*
